newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kingspan makes acquisition, sets right issue.
newsitem.headline: Kingspan makes acquisition, sets right issue.

text.p: Kingspan Group Plc said on Thursday that it had agreed to acquire the business and certain assets of Ward Building Systems and the entire issued share capital of Atlas Bausysteme GmbH from Rugby Group for an initial consideration of 25.9 million sterling.
Kingspan also announced a 1-for-6 rights issue at a price of 440 Irish pence per share to raise around 20.42 million punts before expenses.
The balance of the consideration will be met from borrowings, Kingspan said in a statement.
Adjustment will be made with reference to the value of net operating assets of Ward at the date on which the acquisition becomes effective.
Kingspan said it believed that the total consideration payable was unlikely to exceed 26.5 million punts and that the acquisition would be earnings neutral in 1997 and earnings enhancing thereafter.
Ward is principally involved in the manufacture of building components, steel structures and pre-fabricated metal buildings.
Kingspan said it believed the acquisition would assist it to maintain its competitive position and enhance opportunities for export business.
"The acquisition will also complement the existing Kingspan business and provide the opportunity to achieve synergies and economies of scale," the company said.

Kingspan said it would review the future of the structures division -- Atlas (UK) and Atlas Germany -- in the short term as this division is involved in contracting which is not a core business of Kingspan.

The acquisition is conditional on shareholder approval but irrevocable undertakings to vote in its favour have been given by Eugene Murtagh, Brendan Murtagh and Eoin McCarthy in respect of 51.3 percent of Kingspans existing share capital.
Kingspans directors also said they believed that a wider shareholder base was appropriate for the company at this stage of development.
With a view to broadening the shareholder base, both Eugene and Brendan Murtagh will renounce their beneficial entitlements under the rights issue.
